full_judgment: 26. The present petitioner was one of the third parties in the above proceeding. The respondent No. 4 was not, however, a party to the said proceeding and as such, the order in this proceeding did not bind him, but it is relevant at least as evidence of possession of the petitioner at the time when the order was passed. The order in this proceeding was unsuccessfully challenged in Criminal Motion No.111(1) of 1957 before the learned Sessions Judge, Bakerganj, and ultimately before the High Court in Criminal Revision No. 547 of 1957. Thereafter, the respondent No. 4 instituted Title Suit No. 191 of 1959 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal, against the petitioner and others for establishment of title and khas possession in the disputed lands and this suit is still pending as Title Suit No. 10 of 1984 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Bhola. In this suit the petitioner and others filed an application for injunction for restraining the respondent No. 4 and the other plaintiffs of that suit from entering on the disputed lands and this application was allowed and the respondent No. 4 and the other plaintiffs were restrained from entering into the disputed lands by an order dated 17.11.60 as at Annexure 'C'. The respondent No. 4 then filed an application for temporary injunction against the respondent No. 3, the Deputy Commissioner of Bhola, who was the defendant No. 1 in that suit, for restraining him from disturbing the alleged possession of the respondent No. 4 and the prayer was allowed by the learned Subordinate Judge and the order of the Subordinate Judge was affirmed by the learned District Judge. The orders of the Subordinate Judge and the District Judge were reversed by the High Court Division of the Supreme Court in Civil Revision No. 25 of 1985 on 29.5.85 and the prayer of the respondent No. 4 was rejected finding that the respondent No. 4 and the other plaintiffs of the suit had no possession in the disputed lands till 1960. A petition for special leave to appeal being Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal No. 149 of 1985 was filed before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court and was rejected by their Lordships of the Appellate Division. The order is at Annexure "E". His Lordship Shahabuddin Ahmed, J, as his Lordship was then, speaking for the Court observed "Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the petitioner, has made strenuous efforts to convince us that the petitioners have been in possession all along on the basis of their settlement from the Ulania Joint Estate. But we find no evidence of any settlement from the ex-landlords. The suit land was recorded as Government khas land. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed contends that this entry in the khatian is wrong in that the suit land was found by the Settlement Officer and the Pleader Commissioner to be included in "Udaypur Mouza." But whether the land falls within Udaypurmouza or Char Sitarammouza, there is no dispute about its identity and it is found to be the one and the same land, which is the bone of contention between the parties. In the absence of any prima facie prbof of the settlement from the ex-landlords, the petitioners are trying to make out a case that if the land appertains to Udaypurmouza it will necessarily follow that it was the former Zaminders to the petitioners (sic.) As to possession, in a previous proceeding under section 145 CrPC MR Case No. III of 1954 lessees of the Zaminders were not found in possession. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed contends that in that proceeding the petitioners were not parties; but there is no dispute that the said proceeding was instituted in respect of this very land though it was filed by another set of claimants, and it is after the disposal of this proceeding that these petitioners filed the Title Suit claiming title and possession in respect of the same land. In these circumstances, the High Court Division prima facie found that the plaintiffs got no possession in the suit land and on that finding set aside the order of temporary injunction. We do not find any wrong in the finding of the High Court Division."
